Round 5 answer to L4-8: accept. Already inside the HL-2 signature, and recorded there as the agent's least confident recommendation. The weighed alternative, adding a verb that blocks until an agent finishes, was flagged on the card as voiding the HL-2 signature and re-packeting the verb set; the human did not reopen it.

Round R-4

R-4 · human — HL-1 Persistence is signed: the run manifest file, one agent entry, one knowledge-store entry, and the identity, concurrency, retention and evolution table, exactly as the packet stated them.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 4 answer to HL1-1: sign, with no note attached, so the quote is the mark itself. No approving sentence was written and none is invented here. Signing settled three rows the packet marked as the agent's rather than quoted from a criterion, because the requirements were silent on each: the process identifier, without which AC-013 cannot kill anything it names; a proposed meaning for the word ground, which AC-018 uses once and never defines; and manifest retention, which no criterion states. It also took as accepted the six risks the packet listed. Any later layer that moves a row voids this signature and the packet returns marked with the delta.

R-4 · human — Environment facts are re-detected each run. Nothing about the machine is promoted to any durable register before the knowledge store is deleted.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 4 answer to L3-6: drop-promotion. This removes a clause from AC-019, which is why it was never the agent's to take. It is consistent with the earlier decision that detection reads the session it is in rather than the machine, on the grounds that what is installed and what is usable are different questions. The alternative the human had proposed in round 3, promoting facts into the layered steering file, was weighed on the card and lost on two counts: the fact would be prose an agent reads rather than data a program reads, and every promotion would cost a human approval, so an unattended run could promote nothing.

Round R-3

R-3 · human — The run manifest is keyed by feature alone. The owning contact session is a field inside it, which adoption rewrites.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 3 answer to L3-3: feature-only. This is a ruling on a requirement contradiction, not a design preference. AC-012 keys the manifest by feature identifier and contact session; AC-015 requires a later contact agent to adopt that manifest rather than start a second one. A key holding the old session never matches a new one, so the two could not both hold. The ruling keeps AC-015 whole and edits the key in AC-012, which now reads as an attribute rather than part of the key.

R-3 · human — AC-019's promotion clause is dropped. Environment facts are re-detected each run and nothing about a machine is carried forward.

What settled it
Evidence
Asked in round 3, answered in round 4 as card L3-6: drop-promotion. It stayed open across one round on purpose. The round 3 answer was a write-in naming the repository's layered context harness as the durable register, which contradicted a claim the agent had made. Rather than apply it or dismiss it, the claim was checked and the card re-asked with what the check found. The human was right that the harness is real, layered and stewarded with their own approval on every write. The agent was right that no section shape in it holds a machine fact and that no script reads those files back as data. One part of the write-in was wrong and was corrected on the card: the Codex-side file is not a write target, because no skill writes it.

R-3 · agent — The knowledge store is deleted by the same explicit cleanup step that closes the desktop tool terminals, rather than by a new trigger of its own.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 3 answer to L3-5: accept, audited. The step it rides on already exists for another reason, so this adds an action rather than a trigger. The accepted loss is on the record and unchanged: a session that is killed never reaches the step, so the store survives until the next run for that feature overwrites it.
Audit
explicit

Round R-2

R-2 · human — The transport verb set is signed: six verbs, inherited answer shapes, a declared time budget and repeat behaviour per verb, and input as a positional argument.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 2 answer to HL2-1: sign, with no note attached, so the quote is the mark itself. No approving sentence was written and none is invented here. Signing took as accepted the four risks the packet named and its three weighed alternatives, including the one the agent named as its least confident: polling for status rather than a blocking wait verb. Any later change to the verb set voids this signature and it is re-packeted.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 2 answer to L3-1: agent-dir. It was a call rather than a recommendation because the alternative needed a new ignore rule for the documentation tree, and ignore rules are repository configuration that this feature's own access policy forbids any agent to write.

R-2 · agent — The manifest is written under a directory mutex and replaced by writing a temporary file and renaming it, so no reader sees a half-written kill list.

What settled it
Evidence
Both halves are existing house patterns: maven-lock.sh:1-65 is a directory mutex with stale-lock theft and exit traps, and gate-cache.sh:83-93 writes temp-then-rename with a comment saying the purpose is to stop a reader seeing a torn key. Accepted in round 2.

explicit

Round R-1

R-1 · human — A run outlives its contact session. A later contact agent adopts it by feature id plus contact session and continues the work.

What settled it
Evidence
Round 1 answer to L1-1: durable-run, no note. This closed session-end teardown as an option before card L2-2 was reached, because a run meant to survive its session must not be ended by the session ending.

R-1 · agent — The plugin starts and owns processes the harness does not know about, each wrapped in an operating-system job whose close ends the whole tree.

What settled it
Evidence
Requirement decision 0007 states that registration alone is not cleanup. A live trial on this machine killed a parent and watched its child and grandchild keep running, so the job object is the guarantee and the manifest is the report. Accepted in round 1.

explicit

What settled it
Evidence
Round 1 answer to L1-3: accept. Every transport in the catalog starts a local process, a local pane or a local terminal, and none needs a port or a second host.

R-1 · agent — Transport becomes a fifth adapter family, one kind per transport, beside tracker, forge, notes and build gate.

What settled it
Evidence
The registry check derives families from the adapters directory listing at adapter_registry_check.py:41-46, and the dispatcher builds its path from the family string with no set check at adapter.sh:37-52. Only scripts/afk-config.py and CONFIG.md must change. Accepted in round 1.

explicit

What settled it
Evidence

Evidence

claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to MANIFEST, install_block over the name forms this pass searched
/afk:setup loads the whole register at run time and offers every opt-in row in the step-3 election on every branch, deselected by default; a declined row reports skipped (user choice).

Step 4 runs auto: fixes and asks first only for global installs (npm i -g, pip install) in an interactive session; human: fixes are walked through with the human and every touched entry is probed again.
Setup states no rule for a run with no human present; an opt-in row is skipped then only because it stays deselected by default.

install_block.py install replaces or appends the one afk:behaviors block and removes duplicate unified blocks and the H7, H8 and H10 legacy blocks; teardown removes every named block; both keep all outside bytes and write atomically under an OS lock.
/afk:setup teardown runs install_block.py teardown on the two user instruction files and nothing else, so it removes managed blocks only and uninstalls no tool.
A multiplexer row whose uninstall note points at /afk:setup teardown would state something false unless the teardown branch gains an uninstall step, which the design does not plan.
H7 renders BEHAVIORS.md through behavior_registry.py render against each enabled provider target's own root and installs it with install_block.py install; teardown is named in its note.

set_instruction_files.py merges exactly pluginConfigs."agents-md@builtin".options.instructionFiles into the Claude settings file, backs it up first, and writes no permission key; no setup script writes a permissions key.
citations: git grep -n -I -E -e permissions -e '"allow"' -- skills/afk/setup scripts hooks/lib/providers (exit 0: only test names and provider tool_class lists)

claims.text: The register already holds an opt-in multiplexer row, C15 herdr, which says no skill invokes it and carries no uninstall command; adding a second herdr row would break the one-entry-per-dependency rule, so change (a) has to edit C15.
Audit check 2 searches only skills/, hooks/ and agents/, so a first invoker under adapters/ or scripts/ does not stop it reporting the multiplexer row as unreferenced.

Native-contract check A scans MANIFEST.md with the other plugin markdown and refuses Claude Code or Codex there unless hooks/native-contract-allow.txt carries a matching line; a row naming no harness, in the H11 form, passes.

Registry check C needs an E-table row for an upper-case variable that hooks read but never assign; a rule constant assigned in hooks/lib/providers/claude.sh needs none, and a self-default assignment counts as a read and blocks Stop.
Registry check E refuses an adapter.json register id with no matching `### <id> · ` heading; the C15 heading exists.
The behavior registry gate's parity check needs MANIFEST.md to mention afk:behaviors and the 3 legacy sentinels and test_install_block.py to define 3 named tests; neither new row changes that.
The genericity gate refuses a ticket-shaped token such as AUTO-1 in an added register line unless hooks/genericity-allow.txt lists it.
No test runs the doctor loop, the election or the teardown branch; install_block.py, set_instruction_files.py and the three register gates are pinned by their own tests.
The register carries the id H12 twice, at MANIFEST.md:294 and :334.
What the multiplexer's vendor installer and uninstall change on a machine, and whether the harness accepts the printed allow rule, lie outside the repository.

The seed's hit set misses sites that reach the register or install_block with no MANIFEST or install_block name in the line: row-id phrases, adapter register arrays, sentinel and settings keys, and content scans over every plugin *.md

Native contract gate checks A and K read skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md by content: check A refuses a line naming Claude Code or Codex without a line-specific allow entry, check K refuses a line naming a hooks/lib/providers/<name>_*.py helper; both are pinned by the copy-of-tree test

Change (b) leaves check A and check K passing only if the row names no harness and calls the provider file through claude.sh or provider.sh; that is what design row C19 plans, and a row text naming Claude Code would need an allow entry in hooks/native-contract-allow.txt in the same commit

Eleven adapters/*/adapter.json files name register rows by id in a `register` array, and skill-registry-gate check E requires each id as a `### <id> · ` heading; a missing row blocks, a row with no adapter naming it does not

/afk:setup teardown removes only managed sentinel blocks from the two user instruction files and runs no row's uninstall command, so an uninstall note that points at /afk:setup teardown would not remove the multiplexer

The register already holds an opt-in multiplexer row with no harness name and no uninstall note (C15 · herdr, MANIFEST.md:594-610), and its binary already has an invoker outside skills/ (scripts/afk-move.py:256)

Audit check 2 greps only skills/, hooks/ and agents/, so an invoker under scripts/ or adapters/ is outside its sweep and 'the row lands with its first invoker or audit reports it unreferenced' is not a mechanical guard

No line under hooks/, scripts/ or skills/afk/setup/ reads or writes a harness permission rule: the search for `permissions` there returned 2 lines, a tooltip and a file-mode test; set_instruction_files.py rewrites the whole Claude settings file but carries every other key over unchanged
citations: git grep -n -I -E -e permissions -- hooks scripts skills/afk/setup ':(exclude,glob)**/investigations/INV-*/**' (exit 0, 2 lines)

claims.text: Register row ids are not unique today: two rows carry the id H12, and check E matches a heading with re.search, so a new row reusing an id is not refused by the readers read here

A run with no human never accepts an opt-in row because the election deselects opt-in rows by default; SKILL.md states no separate no-human rule, so the report label is `skipped (user choice)`; only a live headless run would confirm it
set_instruction_files.py has no lock and no compare between its read and its write, so a human edit of the Claude settings file in that window would be lost

scripts/tests/test_native_contract_events.py:57 runs the whole native-contract gate over a copy of the working tree, and check A scans skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md for harness words, so the test pins that a new register row names no harness; C15 and C19 as designed name none, so the test stays green.

The /afk:setup teardown branch at skills/afk/setup/SKILL.md:27 removes only managed behavior blocks; no subtask's Scope edits it, C15's note carries the multiplexer's own uninstall command, and C19 writes no rule, so the line stays true.

Inference: a C19 register row that writes the words Claude Code in MANIFEST.md turns the native-contract gate and test_native_contract_events.py:57 red unless hooks/native-contract-allow.txt gains an entry, a file no subtask Scope names.
